**MURIALE'S**

**ITALIAN KITCHEN**

| **HEALTH INSPECTION SUCCESS PROGRAM** |
|---|

*Daily habits. Consistent verification. Better inspection performance.*

# Program Control

| **Program Owner** | Kitchen Operations Manager / Person in Charge |
|---|---|
| **Applies To** | Kitchen, dish/stewarding, storage, receiving, staff handling food, managers |
| **Primary Goal** | Maintain inspection-ready conditions every day, not only when an inspector arrives |
| **Review Cycle** | Daily execution • Weekly self-inspection • Monthly trend review • Annual program review |

# Program Contents

**1. Program Purpose & Standard**

**2. Responsibilities**

**3. Inspection Rhythm**

**4. Internal Scoring System**

**5. Inspection Focus Areas**

**6. Corrective Action Standard**

**7. Training & Coaching Program**

**8. Inspection-Day Response**

**9. Records & Documentation**

**10. Monthly Management Review**

**Appendix A - Daily Inspection-Readiness Check**

**Appendix B - Weekly Full Self-Inspection**

**Appendix C - Corrective Action Record**

**Appendix D - Monthly Inspection Performance Review**

**Appendix E - 15-Minute Inspection Readiness Sweep**

| **PROGRAM PRINCIPLE / **We do not “prepare for inspection” on inspection day. The operating standard is that the kitchen should be inspection-ready during every shift. The program is designed to catch small misses early, correct them immediately, and teach the standard while the work is happening. |
|---|

# 1. Program Purpose & Standard

The Health Inspection Success Program establishes a repeatable management system for food-safety and sanitation readiness. It combines daily observations, formal self-inspections, corrective actions, employee training, and trend review so that inspection performance improves through routine execution rather than last-minute cleanup.

## Program objectives

Identify high-risk food-safety and sanitation issues before an inspector does.

Correct critical issues immediately and document what was done.

Build consistent standards across opening, service, closing, receiving, prep, line, storage, and dish operations.

Train employees to recognize inspection risks at their own station.

Use internal inspection data to find repeat problems, weak stations, equipment issues, and training gaps.

Maintain organized records that demonstrate active food-safety management.

| **IMPORTANT / **This is an internal management program and scoring system. It does not replace the current requirements of the local health department, applicable food code, manufacturer instructions, or management policy. Where a legal or regulatory requirement is stricter, the stricter requirement controls. |
|---|

# 2. Responsibilities

| **Role** | **Primary responsibilities** |
|---|---|
| Kitchen Operations Manager / Program Owner | Maintain the program; conduct or assign weekly self-inspections; review trends; create corrective actions; coordinate training; keep inspection records available. |
| Person in Charge / Manager on Duty | Complete opening and mid-shift readiness checks; correct active violations; verify handwashing, temperatures, sanitizer, storage, date marking, and employee practices. |
| Sous Chefs / Shift Leaders | Coach standards in real time; verify station readiness; report repeat issues; make sure corrections survive through service. |
| Cooks / Prep / Dish / Stewarding | Maintain their work area to standard; report unsafe conditions; follow food-safety procedures; correct assigned issues. |
| Maintenance / Brian / Vendors | Correct facility/equipment conditions that affect food safety, sanitation, ventilation, plumbing, pests, refrigeration, or safe operations; provide service records when applicable. |
| All Employees | Speak up when something is wrong. Do not work around food-safety, illness, chemical, equipment, or sanitation problems. |

# 3. Inspection Rhythm

The program uses several inspection layers. Each layer has a different purpose; together they prevent “inspection drift” between formal reviews.

| **Frequency** | **Who** | **Time Required** | **Purpose / Required Actions** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening readiness | Manager / PIC | 5-10 min | Verify hand sinks, refrigeration, hot/cold holding setup, storage, date marking, sanitizer, chemicals, facility condition, and obvious pest/waste issues. |
| Mid-shift spot check | Manager / PIC | 5 min | Observe actual employee practices during production/service: handwashing, glove changes, raw/RTE separation, temperatures, wiping cloths, sanitizer, food protection. |
| Closing verification | Closing manager | 5-10 min | Confirm cleaning, storage, labels/dates, food cooling, trash/waste, chemical control, equipment condition, and corrective actions before the kitchen is left. |
| Weekly full self-inspection | KOM / designated manager | 30-45 min | Complete the full inspection form, score performance, fix critical findings, assign actions, and identify training needs. |
| Monthly management review | KOM + management | 20-30 min | Review scores, repeat findings, overdue corrections, training gaps, equipment/facility risks, and department trends. |
| Pre-inspection / surprise readiness drill | Manager | 15 min | Fast sweep of highest-risk items to verify daily program discipline; not a substitute for routine checks. |

# 4. Internal Scoring System

Use the internal score to measure improvement over time. It is not intended to predict an official health department score. The value is consistency: the same internal rules are applied every week.

| **Finding** | **Meaning** | **Internal deduction** | **Required response** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compliant | Meets Muriale’s standard at time of inspection | 0 | No action; reinforce good practice. |
| Corrected on the spot | Issue found and fully corrected during self-inspection | 1 | Document correction; coach employee if behavior-related. |
| Major out of compliance | Important sanitation, facility, storage, documentation, or operating deficiency | 3 | Assign owner and due date; verify closure. |
| Critical control failure | Immediate food-safety or serious safety risk: illness control, handwashing, unsafe temperatures, cross-contamination, sanitizer failure, sewage, active pest contamination, unsafe chemical/equipment condition, etc. | 5 | Stop affected activity; correct immediately; protect/discard product as required; escalate and document. |

| **TARGETS / **Green: 95-100 with no unresolved critical findings. Yellow: 90-94 or repeat major findings. Red: below 90, any unresolved critical finding, or a pattern showing the standard is not holding between inspections. |
|---|

# 5. Inspection Focus Areas

**Employee health & hygiene:** Illness reporting; clean clothing; hair/beard restraint; wound protection; correct glove use; no eating/smoking in food areas.

**Hand sinks & handwashing:** Accessible hand sinks; hot/cold water; soap; paper towels; correct 20-second wash; wash at required times; no storage in sink.

**Time & temperature control:** Cold holding 41°F or below; hot holding 135°F or above; reheating; cooking; cooling; thermometer availability/accuracy; temperature records.

**Date marking & FIFO:** Muriale’s masking-tape standard: date + initials; older product in front; expired product discarded; no unlabeled stored product.

**Cross-contamination prevention:** Raw below ready-to-eat; clean/sanitized tools; glove/hand changes; safe storage order; separate equipment when needed.

**Cleaning & sanitizing:** Scrape/wash/rinse/sanitize/air dry; food-contact surfaces; sanitizer concentration; test strips; wiping cloth control; clean equipment.

**Food storage & protection:** Food off floor; covered/protected; food-grade containers; packaging intact; dry storage organized; no chemicals over food.

**Receiving:** Product temperature; package condition; frozen condition; expiration; cleanliness; correct items/quantity; reject unacceptable deliveries.

**Facility & equipment:** Floors/walls/ceilings; lighting; ventilation; plumbing; drains; equipment in good repair; refrigeration; leaks; damaged surfaces.

**Pest prevention:** No evidence of insects/rodents; doors tight; sweeps/seals intact; spills/debris controlled; pest findings reported immediately.

**Garbage & waste:** Trash removed; containers clean/covered as appropriate; dumpster lids controlled; grease/waste area managed; no standing water/debris.

**Chemicals & SDS:** Correct labeling/storage; no chemical mixing; approved chemicals only; SDS accessible; PPE and dilution directions followed.

**Employee knowledge / PIC readiness:** Manager can explain illness controls, temperatures, sanitizer, cooling, date marking, corrective actions, allergen handling, and key procedures.

**Records & training:** Temperature, cleaning, corrective action, maintenance, training, inspection, and service records are complete and available.

# 6. Corrective Action Standard

Every inspection finding follows the same management sequence:

STOP the unsafe condition or affected activity when necessary.

FIX the issue immediately when it can be corrected safely.

PROTECT food, guests, and employees; discard or isolate product/equipment when required.

VERIFY the correction actually restored compliance.

DOCUMENT the finding, correction, owner, and follow-up when the issue is significant or repeat.

RETRAIN when the root cause is knowledge, habit, or supervision.

ESCALATE maintenance, vendor, staffing, purchasing, or management issues that cannot be closed at shift level.

| **Finding type** | **Examples** | **Close-out expectation** |
|---|---|---|
| Immediate / critical | No soap at hand sink; unsafe TCS temp; raw contamination risk; sanitizer unavailable; sewage backup; sick food employee | Correct before affected operation continues. Document and escalate. |
| Same-shift major | Unlabeled product, improper storage, dirty food-contact surface, chemical storage problem, missing wiping-cloth sanitizer | Correct during shift and verify before close. |
| Planned corrective action | Damaged tile, door sweep, recurring equipment leak, replacement need, vendor/pest issue | Create corrective action/work order with owner and target date; track to closure. |

# 7. Training & Coaching Program

The Training_Images library should be used as part of active coaching, not simply stored as posters. Each weekly self-inspection should generate training when a repeated or significant finding appears.

| **Training method** | **How to use it** |
|---|---|
| Station coaching | Correct the issue where it happens. Explain what the standard is, why it matters, and what “right” looks like. |
| Chef Toolbox Talk | Use a 5-10 minute focused talk for repeat findings, seasonal risk, new procedures, or inspection preparation. |
| Training images | Post/print topic-specific images at appropriate stations and use them during pre-shift coaching. |
| Hands-on verification | Have employee demonstrate handwashing, thermometer use, sanitizer testing, storage/FIFO, cleaning, equipment safety, etc. |
| Retraining signoff | Use for repeated noncompliance, significant food-safety issue, or formal procedure retraining. |

**Priority inspection training image topics:** Health Inspection Success Program; Hand Sinks & Handwashing; Time & Temperature Control; Date Marking & FIFO; Cross-Contamination Prevention; Cleaning & Sanitizing; Employee Health & Hygiene; Facility/Pest/Waste Control; Receiving Temperatures; Thermometer Calibration; Sanitizer/Test Strips; Safe Cooling; Allergen Cross-Contact Prevention.

# 8. Inspection-Day Response

| **RULE / **Do not hide, falsify, back-date, move, or manufacture records for an inspection. Correct real conditions, answer accurately, provide requested records, and document the inspector’s findings for follow-up. |
|---|

**☐** Notify the manager/PIC and Kitchen Operations Manager when the inspector arrives.

**☐** Have one knowledgeable manager accompany the inspector when appropriate.

**☐** Keep normal safe operations running; do not create chaos by overreacting.

**☐** Correct simple conditions immediately when allowed and practical.

**☐** Record every inspector finding, location, item involved, and any correction made.

**☐** Ask for clarification when a finding or required correction is not understood.

**☐** Collect the inspection report and any supporting documents before the visit is closed.

**☐** Enter all follow-up items into the Corrective Action system and assign owners/dates.

**☐** Conduct a brief post-inspection management review the same day or next business day.

# 9. Records & Documentation

| **Record** | **Minimum program use** |
|---|---|
| Daily readiness checks | Demonstrate ongoing verification and identify recurring shift issues. |
| Weekly self-inspections | Primary internal score and trend source. |
| Corrective action records | Track significant findings through verified closure. |
| Temperature records | Support active time/temperature control. |
| Cleaning/sanitation records | Support scheduled cleaning and correction of missed tasks. |
| Training/toolbox talk records | Show instruction, retraining, and employee participation. |
| Maintenance/PM/work-order records | Support facility/equipment correction history. |
| Vendor/pest/service records | Document outside service and recurring facility risks. |
| Health department inspection reports | Keep current and historical reports with corrective follow-up. |

# 10. Monthly Management Review

Once each month, review inspection performance as an operating metric. The goal is to identify patterns before they become inspection findings.

**☐** Average weekly internal inspection score for the month.

**☐** Any critical findings and whether they were closed immediately.

**☐** Top three repeat findings.

**☐** Stations or shifts with repeat problems.

**☐** Open corrective actions and overdue items.

**☐** Maintenance/facility conditions affecting sanitation or food safety.

**☐** Training completed and retraining still needed.

**☐** Vendor/pest/chemical/service issues affecting compliance.

**☐** Changes needed to SOPs, checklists, pars, storage layout, equipment, or supervision.

**☐** One to three improvement priorities for the next month.

# Appendix A - Daily Inspection-Readiness Check

Complete at opening; use the same list for a quick mid-shift recheck when needed.

| **Cold holding** | TCS cold foods maintained at 41°F or below; equipment functioning; temps recorded. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |  |
| **Hot holding** | Hot foods maintained at 135°F or above; equipment functioning; temps recorded. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |  |
| **Cooking/reheating** | Required internal temperatures achieved; thermometer used correctly. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |  |
| **Cooling** | Cooling method, pan depth, airflow, time/temperature checks and records acceptable. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |  |
| **Date marking/FIFO** | Muriale’s tape system used consistently; product rotated; expired/unlabeled food corrected. | ☐ | ☐ | ☐ |  |

title: New Hire Kitchen Orientation Program
body:
**MURIALE’S ITALIAN KITCHEN**

**NEW HIRE KITCHEN ORIENTATION PROGRAM**

*Back-of-House Onboarding • Safety • Food Safety • Muriale’s Standards*

| **Purpose: Give every new kitchen employee the same clear starting point before station-specific training begins.** |
|---|

This program covers kitchen and back-of-house orientation after the employee has completed the hiring/HR process. Hire365 and Kim’s HR process remain responsible for employment paperwork and HR onboarding such as W-4, I-9, payroll, and other personnel documents. This program starts with the employee’s operational introduction to Muriale’s kitchen.

| **Program Owner** | Kitchen Operations Manager / Kitchen Leadership |
|---|---|
| **Applies To** | Cooks, prep, dish/stewarding, receiving-support, and other BOH employees |
| **Initial Orientation** | First shift / first day |
| **Full Orientation Target** | Complete core signoffs during the first 5–10 working shifts, then continue station competency training |

# 1. Program Structure

The new-hire orientation is intentionally split into three levels so the employee is not overloaded on the first day.

| **Orientation Level** | **Purpose** |
|---|---|
| **Level 1 — First Shift Orientation** | Where things are, who to report to, basic safety, handwashing, illness reporting, food-safety fundamentals, emergency expectations, and the rules that must be followed immediately. |
| **Level 2 — First Week Core Training** | Sanitation, labeling/date marking, FIFO, temperature control, storage, allergen awareness, chemicals, cleaning systems, inspection readiness, waste control, and equipment expectations. |
| **Level 3 — Station / Job Competency** | Hands-on training for the employee’s actual position and equipment. The employee is observed performing the work and signed off when competent. |

# 2. Responsibilities

## Kitchen Leadership / Trainer

Give the new hire a structured orientation instead of relying on whoever happens to be working.

Explain Muriale’s standards and demonstrate the correct method.

Do not sign off a task merely because it was discussed; observe the employee perform required skills.

Correct unsafe or incorrect habits immediately.

Document completed orientation and any retraining needed.

Ensure the employee knows who to ask when unsure.

## New Employee

Ask questions when a procedure, product, label, chemical, or piece of equipment is unclear.

Follow food-safety and safety rules even when the kitchen is busy.

Report unsafe equipment, food-safety problems, illness symptoms, injuries, spills, leaks, and other concerns immediately.

Do not operate equipment that has not been explained or demonstrated.

Accept coaching and demonstrate the standard before being signed off.

# 3. First Shift Orientation

The first shift should focus on immediate safety, food-safety expectations, and how the employee functions inside Muriale’s. Station production training can begin after these basics are covered.

## A. Welcome & Chain of Command

☐ Introduce the employee to the Kitchen Operations Manager, sous chef/manager on duty, key cooks/prep staff, and dish/stewarding team.

☐ Explain who the employee reports to during the shift and who their primary trainer or manager on duty is.

☐ Explain how questions, call-offs, lateness, schedule concerns, injuries, and operational problems are communicated.

☐ Show employee entrances/exits, break expectations, personal-item storage, restrooms, and designated eating/drinking areas.

## B. Kitchen Tour

☐ Front line and back line

☐ Prep area

☐ Walk-ins, reach-ins, and freezers

☐ Dry storage

☐ Dish/stewarding area

☐ Chemical/janitorial storage

☐ Hand sinks and mop sink

☐ Trash/grease areas

☐ First aid, fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and emergency reference/binder locations

☐ LOTO/out-of-service tags and where maintenance issues are reported

## C. Immediate Food-Safety Rules

☐ Wash hands correctly and use hand sinks only for handwashing.

☐ Gloves do not replace handwashing; change gloves between tasks and when contaminated.

☐ Report vomiting, diarrhea, jaundice, fever with sore throat, or infected/open wounds to management immediately.

☐ Keep raw animal foods separated from ready-to-eat foods.

☐ Cold TCS food: 41°F or below. Hot holding: 135°F or above.

☐ Use a clean, sanitized thermometer when a temperature must be verified.

☐ Never serve food you believe may be unsafe; stop and get a manager.

## D. Muriale’s Date Marking / FIFO Standard

☐ Use one strip of masking tape.

☐ Write the date and the initials of the person who prepared/opened/labeled it.

☐ Place older product where it will be used first; newer product goes behind it.

☐ Unlabeled or questionable product must be corrected or brought to a manager before use.

☐ Do not create your own labeling system unless directed by management.

# 4. Kitchen Safety Orientation

| **STOP • MAKE SAFE • REPORT** |
|---|

## Knife & Cut Safety

☐ Use the correct knife for the task and a stable cutting board.

☐ Keep knives sharp and handles clean/dry.

☐ Never place knives loose in sinks or hidden under towels/food pans.

☐ If a knife falls, step back—do not try to catch it.

☐ Report cuts immediately and protect wounds according to food-safety requirements.

## Burn / Heat / Steam Safety

☐ Assume pans, handles, oven doors, and equipment surfaces may be hot.

☐ Use dry towels or proper heat protection.

☐ Open lids and steam equipment away from the body.

☐ Call out 'hot', 'behind', 'corner', or similar kitchen warnings as appropriate.

## Slip / Trip / Fall Prevention

☐ Clean spills immediately or guard the area until it can be cleaned.

☐ Keep aisles, exits, receiving paths, and floor drains clear.

☐ Do not leave boxes, cords, hoses, mats, or tools where they create a trip hazard.

☐ Wear required slip-resistant footwear.

## Equipment Safety

☐ Do not operate unfamiliar equipment until trained.

☐ Never bypass guards, switches, interlocks, or safety devices.

☐ If equipment is damaged, malfunctioning, sparking, leaking, overheating, or otherwise unsafe: stop using it and notify management.

☐ Respect equipment marked OUT OF SERVICE or LOCKED OUT. Do not remove tags, reconnect, reset, or operate it.

☐ Only authorized/trained employees perform Lockout/Tagout; electrical verification is for qualified personnel when required.

## Chemical Safety

☐ Use only approved chemicals.

☐ Read the label and follow required dilution/PPE instructions.

☐ Never mix chemicals.

☐ Keep chemicals labeled and stored away from food and food-contact items.

☐ Know where SDS information and the Chemical Spill/Exposure Response Sheet are located.

☐ Report spills or exposure immediately.

# 5. Food Safety & Sanitation Core Training

## Handwashing & Glove Use

☐ Wash before starting work and whenever hands may be contaminated.

☐ Wash after restroom use, touching face/hair/body, raw food, trash, eating/drinking/smoking, cleaning, and other contamination.

☐ Scrub with soap for at least 20 seconds as trained.

☐ Change gloves between raw and ready-to-eat tasks and when torn, dirty, or contaminated.

## Temperature Control

☐ Know 41°F or below for cold holding and 135°F or above for hot holding.

☐ Know that cooking, cooling, and reheating have separate requirements; ask if unsure.

☐ Use the probe thermometer correctly and sanitize it before/after use.

☐ Notify management immediately when food or equipment is out of range.

## Cold Storage Order & Cross-Contamination

☐ Ready-to-eat foods and produce above raw animal foods.

☐ Raw products arranged to prevent drips/leaks and cross-contamination.

☐ Keep food covered/protected and off the floor.

☐ Do not place chemicals, personal items, or contamination hazards with food.

## Cleaning vs. Sanitizing

☐ Cleaning removes food/soil; sanitizing reduces microorganisms after cleaning.

☐ Food-contact sequence: wash, rinse, sanitize, air dry.

☐ Do not towel-dry sanitized food-contact items.

☐ Keep wiping cloths in the correct sanitizer solution when required.

## Sanitizer & Test Strips

☐ Use the correct sanitizer for the station/task.

☐ Use test strips appropriate to the chemical.

☐ Do not guess sanitizer strength.

☐ Replace sanitizer when dirty, weak, or otherwise out of standard.

☐ Ask a manager if the required concentration is not known.

## Allergen Awareness

☐ Treat allergy orders seriously and notify/confirm with the chef or manager.

☐ Use clean/sanitized tools, surfaces, utensils, pans, and gloves as directed.

☐ Do not guess whether an ingredient contains an allergen.

☐ Prevent cross-contact and communicate clearly through the whole order.

# 6. Muriale’s Operating Standards

These expectations are specific to how Muriale’s wants the kitchen operated. They should be reinforced during the first week and then through normal coaching.

| **Muriale’s Standard** | **Expectation** |
|---|---|
| **Date tape** | Single strip of masking tape with date + employee initials. |
| **FIFO** | Older usable product first; newer product behind. Do not bury old product. |
| **Cold storage** | Follow safe storage order and protect ready-to-eat food from raw product. |
| **Sanitation** | Clean first, sanitize second; sanitizer is verified with test strips. |
| **Inspection readiness** | Operate as though an inspector could walk in at any time. Do not wait for inspection day to correct routine issues. |
| **Corrective action** | If you see a problem: stop/fix what you can, protect food/people, tell a manager, document when required, verify the fix. |
| **Equipment** | Unsafe or failed equipment is taken out of service and tagged. Do not work around a safety device or remove a tag. |
| **Maintenance** | Report equipment and facility issues early to a manager. Do not wait for complete failure or try to work around an unsafe condition. |
| **Clean-as-you-go** | Do not allow debris, spills, utensils, boxes, or dirty equipment to accumulate unnecessarily. |
| **Communication** | Call out hazards, hot pans, behind/corner movement, low stock, failed equipment, food-safety concerns, and other operational issues. |
| **Staff meals** | Follow the current staff-meal plan and assigned responsibilities without interfering with guest service. |

# 7. First Week Orientation Plan
